proposed_usage: advisory high-risk decision stage for feature-card and release/security review packets
tools.gap: High-impact workflows lacked a durable independent-review receipt and explicit advisory-versus-binding decision boundary.
tools.risk: Mock receipt is unsigned and advisory; production binding requires Tribunal signature/trust-policy verification and an explicit human approval policy.
tools.reason: The dedicated gate runs a mock panel, verifies the persisted artifact set, and emits the versioned decision receipt without claiming quorum or binding approval beyond the fixture. The 2026-08-12 Tribunal regression work did not expand the workflow's advisory boundary.
tools.rollback: Remove the optional advisory gate and retain the existing evidence packet; no workflow completion depends on the unsigned mock decision.

proposed_usage: durable handoff for agent-backed feature cards and resumable workflow stages
tools.gap: Existing workflows had no reusable pause/resume handoff with correlated event/receipt export and explicit delivery semantics.
tools.risk: Relay is a hardened local alpha; this integration proves local persistence, provider-tool execution through bounded policy workers, and operator resume, not remote exactly-once delivery or authenticated service durability. The 2026-08-12 Relay backlog refresh did not expand workflow-catalog guarantees.
tools.reason: The dedicated workflow runs a worktree mission through pause/resume, validates the integrity-checked export, and emits versioned message and delivery receipts. Relay v1.1.0 hardening/refactor commits preserve local persistence and delivery semantics without expanding this workflow boundary.
tools.rollback: Keep existing direct runners; remove the optional Relay handoff and retain the local run packet.

proposed_usage: retain as provider-normalization and fixture/live boundary owner
tools.gap: None identified for current catalog; recent AI SDK evidence remains focused on provider contracts, regression gates, and fixture/live boundaries owned by AI SDK.
tools.risk: Live-provider validation remains credential- and spend-gated; downstream workflows must not duplicate provider preference routing tables.
tools.reason: The cataloged benchmark and Watchdog showcase still match AI SDK 1.1.0 fixture/live contracts. Native provider-driver and lockfile package contract work belongs to AI SDK/provider-package adoption and does not add workflow-runner claims here.
tools.rollback: Use fixture mode and record live-provider skip boundaries.

proposed_usage: retain as local multi-provider app and benchmark-pane consumer for provider/tool workflows
tools.gap: No catalog migration required; current AI Chat evidence improves capability guidance outside the current showcase runner.
tools.risk: Browser, web-search, and managed-provider execution require explicit local configuration, credentials, Chromium availability, and artifact review; benchmark quality claims must remain model- and run-qualified.
tools.reason: The current showcase only depends on AI Chat as a Watchdog-routed app surface. Managed Hermes profile, tool-selection, and startup-binding fixes improve the sibling app but do not create a new supported workflow entry.
tests: benchmark:run when app and profile are configured
tools.rollback: Keep the current Watchdog showcase; defer benchmark/tool workflow promotion until a dedicated workflow contract exists.

proposed_usage: retain as local proxy, telemetry, named-upstream, auth/rate-limit, and agent-insights observability layer
tools.gap: None identified for current catalog; recent Watchdog evidence documents audit and regression work without changing the existing fixture-showcase contract.
tools.risk: Production posture requires separate API/proxy tokens, redaction, rate-limit configuration, environment-specific upstream credentials, and dated pricing evidence.
tools.reason: The showcase still routes AI traffic through Watchdog and exports telemetry. Hermes routing and pricing catalog refreshes are compatible sibling evidence and do not require a workflow contract migration.
tools.rollback: Use fixture/local proxy mode and record live upstream skips.

proposed_usage: bounded execution backend for future Workcell-aware Relay missions
tools.gap: Feature and agency workflows lacked a declared container boundary, resource policy, artifact export contract, and completion receipt.
tools.risk: Docker daemon/host kernel remain trusted; Workcell 1.0 is not a microVM or hosted multi-tenant isolation boundary and does not provide scheduling, organization-specific egress enforcement, or compliance certification.
tools.reason: The dedicated gate validates and inspects the Workcell definition, executes or records host-runtime blockage with versioned receipts, and preserves Workcell's documented host and daemon trust boundary. No newer Workcell commit was present this week.
tools.rollback: Continue with current local fixture and Git worktree flows; remove the optional Workcell gate without claiming container isolation.

proposed_usage: continue owning orchestration and paused approval state
tools.gap: None identified for current catalog; persisted workflow resume hardening is compatible with the current workflow and Publishing House pause/resume contracts.
tools.risk: External ChatOps delivery and callback authorization remain deployment-specific.
tools.reason: Existing workflows already exercise the current Dispatch contract, and Publishing House fixture proof covers deterministic offline run state and approval pause/resume. Dispatch 1.2.0 router/runtime hardening and pinned AI SDK release gates preserve the catalog boundary.
tools.rollback: Use local non-interactive Dispatch path.

proposed_usage: retain as failure evidence owner
tools.gap: None identified.
tools.risk: Secrets and large logs must remain redacted/bounded.
tools.reason: Codebase Cleanup reserves Casefile for actual verification failures and does not manufacture bundles on clean runs.
tools.rollback: Keep stage logs without CaseFile bundle.

proposed_usage: retain as execution history owner
tools.gap: None identified; optional writes must not mask finish failures.

tools.reason: Codebase Cleanup exposes RunLedger as a host-owned adapter instead of creating an unrelated task automatically. VideoOps release proof records lifecycle receipts with zero-token fixture accounting.

proposed_usage: repository reconnaissance for cleanup

tools.reason: The cleanup workflow can run Scout read-only and retains independent deletion evidence guards.
tools.rollback: Use repository-native inventory and keep cleanup classification unchanged.

proposed_usage: reviewed architecture boundary evidence
tools.gap: Arbitrary repositories may not have a Fence model.
tools.risk: Invented boundaries would create false cleanup findings.
tools.reason: The integration is applicable only when the target owns fence.toml.
tools.rollback: Skip Fence and preserve architecture as UNKNOWN.

tools.reason: Read-only Concord scan evidence is recorded alongside the cleanup report.
tools.rollback: Use the workflow's conservative missing-path evidence only.

proposed_usage: cleanup batch blast-radius evidence

tools.gap: None identified for fixture proof cards.
tools.risk: Rendered proof cards are evidence artifacts, not publication or distribution.
tools.reason: VideoOps release proof validates and renders Howl fixture artifacts without posting or scheduling external media.
tools.rollback: Keep JSON receipts and skip visual proof-card rendering.

proposed_usage: retain as VideoOps render backend for local HyperFrames compositions
tools.gap: Cloud render and account-backed media effects are outside the fixture contract.
tools.risk: Render correctness depends on local CLI, ffmpeg/ffprobe availability, media rights, and independent review.
tools.reason: The VideoOps HyperFrames stage runs local check/render, ffprobe inspection, revision application, and finalization only after critic PASS.
tools.rollback: Stop at composition and receipt evidence without final render claims.

cross_tool_patterns.reason: The three boundaries now have versioned package, handoff, completion, and decision receipts, but no catalog workflow composes them; Relay and Workcell recovery/scheduling remain bounded local capabilities.
Dispatch already owns current orchestration and approval state; adding Relay would duplicate ownership without a handoff contract.
The advisory decision receipt exists, but feature-card binding policy, participant authority, threshold, dissent handling, and paused-workflow resume ownership still require a product decision.
